Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
CONTEXT / EVIDENCE
Offline PEAK, default PEAK difficulty; last named overlay SHORE — DAY ONE. Handbook goal: reach high ground/nearest peak for rescue. No summit, rescue, checkpoint use, completion or teammate observed. Screenshots are omitted: visual evidence below is prior agent reporting, not fresh image inspection. Completed inputs establish execution, not successful movement. Global position/net elevation remain uncertain; repeated landmarks strongly suggest local loops.

LATEST / ACTIVE GOAL
Last observed: broad pale palm trunk on left; bare orange ground rises ahead beneath purple spikes; dark cleft on right; narrow suspended brown span beyond. Trunk partly bypassed. Recent 0.5 s walking steps reportedly advanced along exposed footing without visible stamina loss. Connection to opposite slope/arch/span remains unconfirmed.
LAST EXECUTED: w alone, duration 0.5 s, no buttons, dx=dy=0; completed. Resulting view has NOT been observed. Active goal remains finding an uphill route/high ground, particularly access near the arch/elevated spans, without repeating enclosed pockets or losing height into clefts. No action selected here.

INVENTORY / CONDITION
Last confirmed numbered inventory: 1 CHECKPOINT FLAG unused; 2 SPORTS DRINK retained, recently stowed with 2; 3 FIRST AID KIT retained; 4 equipped BACKPACK, last inspected containing one ENERGY DRINK. No confirmed drink consumption, healing or later pack-content change. GUIDEBOOK dropped at crash supplies; spare SPORTS DRINK left in second opened palm-side luggage. Regular slots occupied. Green Crispberry was picked up into an extra hand slot despite full numbered slots; later disappeared from hand view after Tab, destination unknown. No item subsequently shown held after stowing Sports Drink.
Green stamina repeatedly recovers to a reduced striped limit; later reports show brown/yellow/red stripes occupying much of bar. Walking usually preserves or restores green stamina. Earlier injury evidence: red vignette, broken-heart icon, red striped segment after ledge attempts. Cause/severity unknown; spikes/fall damage not proven. Rest does not remove red penalty. Other stripe meanings unknown.

CONTROLS / INTERACTIONS
Inputs: keys, buttons, dx/dy, duration; usually 1 s, sometimes 0.5 s. w forward; a/d strafe; diagonals work. s backing away has now exposed more footing/clearance in several views, though global displacement is unknown. Shift_L+w sprints and drains stamina; w+space jumps; diagonal jumps sometimes clear obstacles. wait seconds:1 can restore stamina when supported, sometimes after delay.
Positive dx turns right, negative left; positive dy looks down, negative up. Left/Right and Up/Down also control look. No angular calibration. Large stationary turns sometimes reveal openings hidden by close walls. Control_L+w+a presumed crouch attempt did not establish crouching or an escape.
Number keys equip; pressing selected number again stows while retaining icon, freeing hands (1,2,3 confirmed). Empty-slot selection also worked earlier. j and buttons:[left] are primary-action inputs, with inconsistent engagement in some contexts. q drops held item/pack (guidebook/backpack confirmed); throw untested. Flag primary prompt would plant/use, untested.
E interacts near correctly targeted highlighted objects. Luggage opens with yellow hold-progress ring; repeated 1 s E/lid animation sometimes needed. Pickup timing/aim/capacity requirements are not universal. Escape closed passport customization; number selection did not. Pointer-left works in menus; guidebook scroll steps:1 advanced pages.

ITEM TESTS / UNRESOLVED EFFECTS
Unidentified flat purple oval with dark edge projections repeatedly marks open orange slope near pale column and palms. Earlier E attempt gave no name/prompt/inventory change; not proof unusable or safe. Distinct from pointed purple vegetation.
Yellow-green bush fruit against dark wall, left of large purple spikes, identified by highlight as GREEN CRISPBERRY, E pick up. E put one in extra hand slot; two fruits then visible on bush. Eat prompt appeared. Three separate 1 s left holds produced partial yellow ring, later roughly two-thirds; berry remained. One 1 s J also failed to consume. Tab removed hand slot/eat prompt without visible penalty improvement; storage, hiding or other outcome unconfirmed.
Sports Drink: 2 equipped bottle and drink prompt. Two separate 1 s left holds: first roughly two-thirds yellow ring; later ring vanished but bottle remained, penalties unchanged. 2+w then stowed bottle. First aid previously showed heal injuries; separate 1 s J/J/left attempts gave about one-fifth progress, retained kit and persistent injury. Short holds resetting progress or needing a longer uninterrupted hold are hypotheses, not established. No successful consumption/healing or item effect observed. Earlier Tab merely lowered a drink without proving storage/free capacity.

CLIMBING / FAILED STRATEGIES
Empty-handed w+j or w+space+j previously gave pink hands, chevron, height gain and heavy stamina drain; diagonal grips traversed rock. Actual left sometimes engaged where J only showed ring, but neither universally succeeds. White ring/yellow dot alone do not prove grip or footing; hands alone also appear in ordinary movement.
Tall climbs repeatedly depleted stamina before rims; w+Shift_L+j leap emptied bar/red X without clearing rim. Releasing near crests often lost height. Some short climbs reached flat pale-orange resting footing, not confirmed intended upper ledges.
Recent pale-column test beside broad palm: looking sharply up revealed column tops beneath dark overhang, palm/orange hanging shapes overhead-left. w+space+left initially ring/no hands/slight drain; subsequent w+left showed pink hand/chevron and closer edge; another hold left only green sliver, rim still overhead. Release removed indicators; recovery delayed, then restored on lower footing. No top reached. Palm-trunk climbability unresolved.
Later inside cleft, repeated w+left and w+space+j showed ring/no hands or chevron, little drain/recovery, no sustained grip. Turning/backing away eventually exposed an opening;
